events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.description: East German authorities announced that citizens could cross the border freely, and crowds began streaming through checkpoints between East and West Berlin. Many people climbed on and began dismantling parts of the wall that had divided the city since 1961.
events.significance: The opening of the Berlin Wall became the defining symbol of the end of the Cold War and led to German reunification in October 1990 and the collapse of communist regimes across Eastern Europe.

events.title: Kristallnacht
events.description: On the night of November 9-10, Nazi paramilitaries and civilians attacked Jewish communities throughout Germany, Austria, and the Sudetenland. Synagogues were burned, thousands of Jewish-owned businesses were smashed, and about 30,000 Jewish men were sent to concentration camps.
events.significance: The pogrom marked a sharp escalation in Nazi persecution of Jews and is widely seen as a precursor to the Holocaust.

events.title: Kaiser Wilhelm II Abdicates and Germany Becomes a Republic
events.description: Amid military defeat and revolution at the end of World War I, Chancellor Max von Baden announced the abdication of Kaiser Wilhelm II. Philipp Scheidemann proclaimed a German republic from the Reichstag balcony.
events.significance: The event ended the German monarchy and the Hohenzollern dynasty and created the Weimar Republic, shaping Germany's turbulent interwar history.

events.title: Cambodia Gains Independence from France
events.description: Cambodia achieved full independence from France, following diplomatic campaigning by King Norodom Sihanouk. The date is celebrated as Independence Day in Cambodia.
events.significance: Independence ended decades of French colonial rule in Cambodia and set the stage for the country's complex post-colonial and Cold War history.

events.title: Birth of Carl Sagan
events.description: Carl Sagan, the American astronomer, planetary scientist, and science communicator, was born in Brooklyn, New York. He contributed to NASA missions and wrote and presented the series Cosmos.
events.significance: Sagan popularized science for millions of people worldwide and advanced the study of planetary science and the search for extraterrestrial life.
